title: Hero art: integrate the PixelLab pixel-art hero sprites (AnimatedSprite2D + state-driven AnimationController), replacing the greybox ColorRect
description:
Replace the player's placeholder greybox (Sprite ColorRect + FacingMark ColorRect in scenes/player.tscn) with the real PixelLab pixel-art hero ('technomagical elemental monk', 16-bit McFarlane style, 92x92, side view) currently in the gitignored AssetBundles/character/ (4 PixelLab 'states' = one hero in multiple state sets; see AssetBundles/character/metadata.json). The hero color/aura is cyan and already matches the current ColorRect tint (0.35,0.85,0.95).

DESIGN DECISIONS (confirmed with the human):
- FACING: use the EAST frames only and flip_h by code from Player.facing. Halves the import and sidesteps the fighting_pose west variant-glitch (it has TWO west dirs).
- CAST VISUAL: play the 'attack' animation (cyan burst, 9f) as a brief ONE-SHOT each time a cast fires, then return to the movement animation. Hold-to-fire stays as is.

STATE -> ANIMATION MAPPING (FSM emits StateMachine.state_changed; cast is hold-to-fire in any state):
- Idle (MoveState, on floor, vel.x~0) -> idle-breath 'shifts weight/drawing' (9f, loop)
- Run/Walk (MoveState moving) -> Walking (4f, loop)
- Jump/rise (JumpState, vel.y<0) -> Two-Footed Jump rising frames (one-shot)
- Fall (JumpState, vel.y>0) -> Two-Footed Jump descending frames (no dedicated fall)
- Glide (GlideState) -> NO dedicated anim: fallback to a jump-descend frame or the flight hover (flag as a gap; can be PixelLab-generated later)
- Flight (FlightState) -> fighting_pose 'suspended-mid-air glow' (9f, loop) — best aura
- Cast (on fire) -> attack (9f, one-shot overlay)
- Hurt (take_player_damage lands) -> takedamage (9f) — today only the i-frame blink exists
- Death (respawn) -> NO dedicated anim: fallback to last hurt frame / fade (flag as a gap)

TECHNICAL STEPS:
1. Copy ONLY the used PNGs (east frames + the needed anims) from the gitignored AssetBundles/character/ into assets/sprites/hero/; add a PixelLab credit/license note to assets/CREDITS.md.
2. Import as pixel-art: nearest filter, no mipmaps; reimport the .godot cache.
3. Build resources/hero/hero_frames.tres (SpriteFrames) via a tools/build_hero_frames.gd EditorScript that reads metadata.json and assembles the named animations with fps + loop flags (reproducible, like tools/build_sector_02_tiles.gd).
4. scenes/player.tscn: replace the Sprite ColorRect + FacingMark ColorRect with an AnimatedSprite2D ('Sprite') using hero_frames.tres. CRITICAL: measure the opaque bbox and set offset/INTEGER scale so the feet seat on the bottom of the UNCHANGED 24x40 RectangleShape2D collision (the floor-seating lesson). Collision shape stays BYTE-IDENTICAL.
5. Add scripts/player/animation_controller.gd: listens to state_changed + reads velocity/facing/casting/hurt and selects animation + flip_h. Keep the selection a PURE, unit-testable function (state,vel,facing,casting,hurt)->anim_name.
6. Rewire player.gd: change @onready var _sprite: ColorRect to AnimatedSprite2D/CanvasItem (blink via .visible still works); drive flip_h from facing; fire the attack one-shot on cast; play hurt on a landed hit.
7. Tests + CI: unit-test the mapping function; assert player.tscn loads headless; assert the collision shape is unchanged; GUT crucial(61) + full suites green; gdlint clean.

SAFETY: this is NOT a loose visual tweak — it touches player.gd and adds a testable controller, so FULL ceremony applies (developer tests-first -> reviewer block-on-HIGH -> PR -> CI). Per-frame fps / which-idle / offset fine-tuning afterwards is a DIRECT playtest tweak. Collision/gameplay must be unaffected (movement FSM, combat, corridor metrics all unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: scenes/player.tscn renders the PixelLab pixel-art hero via an AnimatedSprite2D (greybox Sprite/FacingMark ColorRects removed); pixel-art imports with nearest filter (no blur).
The hero animates per the FSM: idle, walk, jump/fall, flight, plus a one-shot 'attack' on cast and a 'hurt' on a landed hit; left/right uses flip_h from Player.facing (east frames only).
The 24x40 RectangleShape2D collision is byte-identical and the hero's feet visually seat on the bottom of the collision box (measured opaque bbox, not eyeballed); movement/combat behavior unchanged.
hero_frames.tres is built reproducibly by tools/build_hero_frames.gd from metadata.json; used PNGs live under assets/sprites/hero/ with a PixelLab credit in assets/CREDITS.md.
The state->animation selection is a pure unit-tested function; player.tscn loads headless; GUT crucial(61) + full suites green; gdlint clean.
Glide and death have NO dedicated PixelLab anim — a documented fallback is used and the gap is noted for a possible later PixelLab generation.
